Jonas / team — initial draft answers below and two artifacts attached. Please review and suggest edits.

Summary bullets (for Acme):
- Subprocessor roster (EU scope): primary cloud providers in EU: GCP (europe-west1), AWS (eu-west-1). Edge/third-party operator providers: EdgeOps Europe Ltd, NodeRun GmbH. See attached operator_roster_eu-20270411.csv and subprocessor_matrix_eu_v2.xlsx.
- Tenant isolation controls:
  * Hosted (standard): logical tenancy with strong cryptographic separation, role-based access controls, customer-scoped KV caches; production tenancy enforced via separate namespaces and token scoping.
  * Dedicated: single-tenant GPU pools in customer VPC or dedicated tenancy; network isolation via VPC peering and dedicated subnet allocations.
  * Private (on-prem/VPC): fully customer-managed networking and optional air-gapped deployment.
- KMS: Customer-managed keys supported for Dedicated and Private; hosted customers may use Redwood-managed KMS unless a dedicated contract is in place.
- Planned operator rotations: We plan a controlled operator roster rotation for one edge operator (NodeRun GmbH -> NodeRun Replacement Partner) in ~60 days for maintenance; this will affect non-Dedicated shared-hosted nodes only. Dedicated and Private customers are unaffected by operator rotations unless explicitly configured. See operator_rotation_mitigation.pdf (attached).

Evidence links included in spreadsheet rows and an internal drive folder: https://drive.redwood/team/compliance/acme-eu-evidence-2027

Attachments: operator_roster_eu-20270411.csv (CSV), subprocessor_matrix_eu_v2.xlsx (Excel)

Let me know if you want us to soften language around caching and fallback routing.

Thanks Marissa — looks solid. A couple of suggested clarifications before we send to Acme:
1) Caching phrasing: call out that prefix/KV caching is namespace-scoped and does not surface data across tenant boundaries. Avoid saying "cryptographic separation" without the word "logical" — prefer "logical cryptographic separation".
2) Fallback routing: include a short note that in case of operator outage we can route to a regional fallback in another EU provider or, only with customer's permission, to a compatible non-EU fallback (us-east) — but emphasize contractual data-residency clauses.
3) Add the operator_rotation_mitigation.pdf (draft attached) and a one-paragraph rollback playbook (short bullets) into the artifacts list.

I'll attach the mitigation doc and a short rollback paragraph to include in the response.

Hi Sarah — thanks for the RFI and the clear ask. Please find our consolidated responses and supporting artifacts below (attachments and evidence links included). I've pasted short Q&A for quick review; full artifacts are attached. Let me know if you'd like a short sync.

Q1 — Current subprocessors/operators in EU (short):
- Cloud infra: Google Cloud (europe-west1), AWS (eu-west-1)
- Edge/Node operators: EdgeOps Europe Ltd (edge compute), NodeRun GmbH (operator nodes)
- Observability/metrics vendor: LogStream EU (EU-hosted)
(See attached operator_roster_eu-20270411.csv and subprocessor_matrix_eu_v2.xlsx for full contacts and roles.)

Q2 — Tenant isolation model and options:
- Hosted: logical tenancy with namespace-scoped cryptographic keys, RBAC, tenant-scoped KV/prefix caches; strong separation between tenant namespaces.
- Dedicated: single-tenant GPU pools deployed into customer VPC or dedicated subnets to provide network-level isolation.
- Private: on-premises packages and VPC deployments are available for full customer control.

Q3 — Customer-managed KMS:
- Supported for Dedicated and Private. Hosted customers can opt into customer-managed keys under an enterprise contract.

Q4 — Planned operator rotations / impact window: 
- We plan a scheduled operator rotation for one shared-edge operator (NodeRun GmbH) in approximately 60 days; this will affect shared-hosted edge lanes only. No rotations planned that affect Dedicated or Private customers by default. We will provide a 30-day notification and mitigation playbook prior to any change.

Evidence / artifacts provided:
- operator_roster_eu-20270411.csv
- subprocessor_matrix_eu_v2.xlsx
- operator_rotation_mitigation.pdf
- internal evidence folder: https://drive.redwood/team/compliance/acme-eu-evidence-2027
- SOC2 report pointer: https://console.redwood.ai/compliance/soc2/report-2026

Sarah — attaching a short rollback playbook (one paragraph) and sending a calendar invite for 2027-04-14 15:00 CEST. Calendar link: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=acme-rfi-sync-20270414

Rollback playbook (summary): In the event an operator rotation causes unexpected service degradation for shared-hosted customers, Redwood will: 1) trigger immediate traffic diversion to pre-warmed fallback nodes in the same geographic region (if available), 2) enforce strict request rate-limiting and queue-length backpressure to protect tenant stability, 3) roll back to the previous operator image and re-provision nodes from snapshots within our rollback window (typically 2-6 hours), and 4) notify affected customers and provide a post-incident timeline. Dedicated and Private customers with single-tenant deployment are not impacted by shared-operator rotations unless explicitly configured.

See attachments and evidence links. Looking forward to the sync.

Thanks,
Jonas
